verdicts.checked: Fetched EMA Qalsody EPAR public assessment report (EMA/276404/2024, 181pp) and located Table 36 'Adverse events by preferred term occurring in 10% or more subjects in any pooled group - data presented for Pool RC and ABCL1 - safety population (as of 15 Jul 2022)'. Row 'Headache': tofersen 100 mg (N=72) 33 (45.8%); placebo (N=36) 16 (44.4%). Numerator, denominator, comparator and cut-off all match exactly. Grade 0 is correct under the at-or-below-control rule.

Same EPAR, Table 37 'Adverse reactions for pooled group ABCL1 - safety population (cut-off 28 Feb 2023)'. Row 'Neuralgia 7/147 (4.8)', frequency category 'Common'. Exact match. ABCL1 is a single-arm pooled tofersen population, so 'no_concurrent_control_arm' is correct.
verdicts.problem: Minor: the row's note asserts the neuralgia was 'non-serious'. Table 37 is an ADR frequency table and does not classify by seriousness; the claim is an inference from the absence of neuralgia from the related-SAE table (Table 38). Not wrong, but not stated at the cited locus.

verdicts.checked: Same EPAR, Table 38 'Related serious adverse events by system organ class and preferred term - safety population (cut-off: 28 Feb 2023)', extracted with pdfplumber to recover the column alignment that plain text extraction garbles. Row 'Intracranial pressure increased': Pool RC1 tofersen 100 mg (N=72) 0; Pool RC2 placebo (N=36) 0; Pool ABCL1 (N=147) 3 (2.0); Pool ABCL2 all doses (N=166) 3 (1.8). readout_value 3_of_147, the 2.0%/1.8% pair, and the placebo 0/36 comparator are all exact. Also confirmed the US label text the note quotes ('Four patients developed elevated intracranial pressure and/or papilledema') in the local DailyMed capture of QALSODY sec 5.2. Grade 2 correct.
verdicts.problem: Worth adding, not an error: the tofersen 100 mg arm of the placebo-controlled period (Pool RC1, N=72) also reported 0 related serious ICP-increased events. All 3 events come from the open-label/earlier-parts pool, which strengthens rather than weakens the row but is not stated.

verdicts.checked: Read the local DailyMed capture of the QALSODY US PI (sources/cns/QALSODY_tofersen_label_dailymed.htm). Section 14 Table 2 'Biomarker Results of QALSODY in Study 1 Part C at Week 28', CSF SOD1 Protein, ITT population N=72/N=36: adjusted geometric mean ratio to baseline 0.65 (QALSODY) and 0.98 (placebo); QALSODY-to-placebo difference in GMR 0.66 (0.57, 0.77); nominal p<0.0001. Every figure matches. Target-protein lowering graded 0 with direction 'decrease' is correct - this is pharmacology, not toxicity.

Fetched the current EXONDYS 51 (eteplirsen) SPL from DailyMed (setid 33bff678-7829-479e-9110-b8e33a0bc0aa) and read sections 5 and 6.2 in full. Section 5 contains only '5.1 Hypersensitivity Reactions'. Section 6.2 Postmarketing Experience lists exactly: bronchospasm, cyanosis of the lips, malaise, pyrexia, flushing, protein urine present, dehydration. No CNS or neurologic warning or postmarketing neurologic reaction anywhere. Dose 30 mg/kg weekly IV confirmed in sec 2.1. Grade 0 label-absence row is correct and the negative control is legitimate.

Fetched the ONPATTRO (patisiran) SPL from DailyMed (setid e87ec36f-...). Section 6.1 Table 1 header reads 'ONPATTRO N=148 % | Placebo N=77 %'; row 'Vertigo | 5 | 1'. Exact match, denominators exact. Vertigo is indeed the only nervous-system-type term in the whole table (the others are URTI, infusion-related reaction, dyspepsia, dyspnea, muscle spasms, arthralgia, erythema, bronchitis). 0.3 mg/kg appears in the label.
verdicts.problem: cns_region is set to 'brainstem'. The label does not localise the event and vertigo of this kind is a peripheral vestibular symptom; MedDRA files it under 'Ear and labyrinth disorders' (confirmed in the APOLLO ClinicalTrials.gov record). Assigning a brainstem locus injects an anatomical claim the source does not make into a CNS dataset.

verdicts.checked: Fetched the TEGSEDI (inotersen) SPL from DailyMed (setid 8513207e-...). Section 5.5 'Inflammatory and Immune Effects', subheading 'Neurologic Serious Adverse Reactions', contains the quoted passage verbatim, including 'elevated protein, a lymphocyte-predominant pleocytosis, and testing that was negative for infection' and 'The patient recovered after empiric therapy (high-dose steroids, antibiotics) and resumed TEGSEDI without recurrence of symptoms'. 284 mg weekly SC dose confirmed in the label. Grade 2, reversible, is correct. is_cns_specific=FALSE is right for a subcutaneously dosed ASO.

Fetched the LEQVIO (inclisiran) SPL from DailyMed (setid 6fc0afca-...). Section 6.1 'Adverse Reactions in Pediatric Patients with HeFH' contains verbatim: 'In pediatric patients with HeFH, the incidence of headache was 6% among patients who received placebo versus 13% of LEQVIO-treated patients during the double-blind study period.' Same paragraph states 141 patients enrolled, 93 received 284 mg LEQVIO in Part 1, 48 switched from placebo - so the placebo denominator of 48 the row flags as derived is arithmetically forced (141-93=48) and the derivation flag is honest. This is indeed the only neurologic imbalance in the label; the adult pooled table (N=1833 vs 1822) lists only injection site reaction, arthralgia and bronchitis. Grade 1 correct.

Downloaded the EMA Spinraza EPAR product information PDF (EU/1/17/1188) and extracted section 4.8 Table 3 'Adverse reactions related to Spinraza administration': Nervous system disorders = Headache** (Very common), Aseptic meningitis (Not known), Arachnoiditis (Not known). Section 4.4 'Lumbar puncture procedure' matches the note verbatim, including the MRI sentence. Cross-checked the US SPINRAZA SPL sec 6.2, which also lists arachnoiditis. 'frequency_not_known' and readout_value TBD are correct.
verdicts.problem: Procedure-vs-drug attribution is incomplete. SmPC section 4.4 introduces arachnoiditis explicitly as 'a risk of adverse reactions occurring as part of the lumbar puncture procedure (e.g. arachnoiditis, headache, back pain, vomiting)'. The row quotes 4.4 but records the event as oligonucleotide neuroinflammation without carrying that procedural attribution into effect_vs_control or the grading rationale. Grade 2 is still defensible for a clinically significant neuro AE, but the row should say the regulator attributes it to the LP procedure.

correction.notes_addendum: EU SmPC sec 4.4 attributes arachnoiditis to the lumbar puncture procedure, not to nusinersen itself; procedural confounding must be assumed.

verdicts.checked: Pulled NCT02623699 from the ClinicalTrials.gov v2 API. otherEvents[106] term='Headache', organSystem='Nervous system disorders': EG006 'Part B-MAD: Cohort 5: BIIB067 20 mg' 4/10 = 40.0%; EG005 'Part B-MAD: Combined Placebo' 7/12 = 58.3%. Exact. Direction 'decrease' and grade 0 are correct - the drug arm is below the concurrent intrathecal-placebo arm, so this is a genuine grade-0 anchor, not manufactured toxicity.
verdicts.problem: The note claims headache was 'at or below the concurrent intrathecal-placebo arm at every dose level'. It was not: EG009 (100 mg) is 6/10 = 60.0%, marginally above the 58.3% placebo rate. 20 mg 40.0%, 40 mg 22.2%, 60 mg 44.4% are all below. The row's own value is unaffected.

correction.notes_correction: headache at or below placebo at 20/40/60 mg; 100 mg was 6/10 (60.0%) vs 58.3% placebo

verdicts.checked: NCT02623699 otherEvents[81] term='Csf protein increased', organSystem='Investigations': EG008 'Part B-MAD: Cohort 7: BIIB067 60 mg' 3/9 = 33.3%; EG005 combined placebo 1/12 = 8.3%. Exact, including the array index. Grade 1 for an isolated CSF-protein elevation with no neuronal loss is correct under the rubric.

NCT02623699 seriousEvents[5] term='Myelitis', organSystem='Infections and infestations': EG011 'Part C-Pivotal: BIIB067 100 mg' 1/72 = 1.4%; EG010 'Part C-Pivotal: Placebo' 0/36. Exact. verdicts.problem: Cosmetic: source_table says 'Eye disorders / Nervous system disorders'. The 'Papilloedema' preferred term sits under Eye disorders only; 'Intracranial pressure increased' is the Nervous system disorders term (seriousEvents[60], 1/32, 1/63, 1/44) and is a separate row.

verdicts.checked: NCT02519036 outcome measure 5 'Change From Baseline in CSF Neurofilament Light Chain Concentration' (ng/L, MEAN with SD). Class 'Change from Baseline': placebo +324 (SD 371, n=12), 10 mg +77, 30 mg +202, 60 mg +274, 90 mg +1161 (SD 2980, n=9), 120 mg +628 (SD 1128, n=10). Class 'Baseline': placebo 2774, 90 mg 2328. Every number in readout_value, effect_vs_control and the note's grade ladder matches exactly, and the note's grade-0 claim for 10/30/60 mg is internally correct (all below the +324 placebo rise). Direction 'increase' with grade 2 is the correct handling of a treatment-emergent NfL rise above concurrent placebo.
verdicts.problem: Not an error, but the row's own caveat understates the problem: with SD 2980 on n=9 the 90 mg mean has a standard error near 1000, so the 837 ng/L excess over placebo is well under one standard error. The grade-2 label at 90 mg rests on a point estimate that is statistically indistinguishable from placebo. The row says so and carries grade_provisional; it should not be consumed as a confident grade 2.

verdicts.checked: NCT02519036 outcome measure 6 'Ventricular Volume as Assessed by Structural MRI' (mL, MEAN/SD). Day 197 60 mg = 34.57 (n=6); Screening 60 mg = 31.90; placebo 35.58 -> 36.46 (n=12). All six curator-computed screening-to-Day-197 changes in the note reproduce exactly from the posted means (placebo +0.88, 10 mg +1.81, 30 mg +1.80, 60 mg +2.67, 90 mg +5.10, 120 mg +5.49). The disclosure that the change is curator-computed and unposted is accurate and important.
verdicts.problem: reversibility='irreversible' is not supportable. Day 197 is a single post-treatment timepoint; the study never followed long enough to establish irreversibility, and the note itself concedes it means only 'no recovery was observed within the study' - with the placebo arm also rising. 'not_assessed' is the honest value.

verdicts.checked: NCT03342053 seriousEvents[12] term='Hydrocephalus', organSystem='Nervous system disorders': EG000 'RO7234292 Monthly' 1/23 (1 event); EG001 'RO7234292 Bimonthly' 0/23. Exact. The 120 mg dose is documented in the record (outcome-measure titles name '120 mg RO7234292'), so the dose attribution is sourced. Both arms received 120 mg, so the dose-frequency framing is right.

The cited locus supports only 'serious hydrocephalus'. Either add the Stoker citation to the provenance chain or drop the grade to 2 with the shunt claim removed. exposure_duration '14mo' matches the arm description; the AE timeframe on the record is 'baseline to up to 18 months'.

correction.source_table_addendum: grade 3 derived from Stoker TB et al., Mov Disord 2021;36(1):263-264, which is not in source_ref

verdicts.checked: NCT03342053 seriousEvents[11] term='Hemiparesis': EG000 'RO7234292 Monthly' 1/23 = 4.3%; EG001 Bimonthly 0/23. Exact. The attribution caveat is well founded: the same arm also reports seriousEvents[10] 'Cerebrovascular accident' 1/23, so the hemiparesis is plausibly the stroke's deficit. verdicts.problem: Internal inconsistency with CMS1289, which cites the same trial: this row records dose TBD while CMS1289 records 120 mg. The record does document 120 mg, so TBD is over-conservative here.

verdicts.checked: NCT03761849 outcome measure 18 'Change From Baseline in CSF Neurofilament Light Chain (NfL) Proteint Level', GEOMETRIC_MEAN with 95% CI, unit as posted 'ng/mL'. Class Week 21: OG002 'RO7234292 Q8W ODC' 16.553 (4.497, 29.999) n=27; OG000 'Placebo ODC' 12.233 (0.729, 25.050) n=28. Exact including denominators. Group description confirms 'RO7234292 120 mg Q8W'. Direction 'increase' is the correct handling and grade 1 rather than 2 for a near-complete CI overlap with placebo is a defensible conservative call.
verdicts.problem: For context, not an error: the much larger NDC cohort at the same visit shows a far cleaner separation (Q8W NDC 31.893 (24.946, 39.226) n=224 vs placebo NDC 3.365 (-2.077, 9.109) n=225). The ODC row alone understates the programme-level CSF NfL signal. The posted unit 'ng/mL' is almost certainly a sponsor typo for pg/mL; the row correctly reproduces what is posted.

verdicts.checked: NCT03761849 otherEvents[19] term='Dizziness': EG003 'Q8W NDC' 20/263 = 7.6%; EG005 'PLB NDC' 17/264 = 6.4%. Exact. Grade 0 correct under the at-or-below-control rule.
verdicts.problem: Data-cut linkage gap: CMS1623 records the same preferred term in the same trial at the CHDI 2021 interim cut (7.7% vs 5.8%, n=260) and is marked 'duplicate_also_in_lane=clinical_programs'; this row carries no reciprocal marker. The two are the same event at two cuts and must not be treated as independent.

verdicts.checked: NCT03761849 seriousEvents[64] term='Demyelination', organSystem='Nervous system disorders': EG003 'Q8W NDC' 1/263 = 0.4% (1 event); EG005 'PLB NDC' 0/264; zero in all four other arms. Exact. Grade 2 with the 'could be 3 if it left a persisting deficit' flag is the right call on an AE table that carries no outcome data.

NCT03842969 (GEN-EXTEND) otherEvents[43] term='Cerebral ventricle dilatation': EG002 'Tominersen 120 mg Q16W' 1/88 = 1.1% (2 events); EG001 Q8W 4/143 = 2.8%; EG000 Q4W 1/14 = 7.1%. All three rates in the note reproduce exactly. No placebo arm exists in this roll-over study, as the row says, and the prior-exposure confound is correctly flagged. verdicts.problem: Minor schema quibble: readout_category is 'imaging' but the source is an investigator-reported adverse-event term, not an imaging measurement; 'clinical_neuro_outcome' would be more faithful.

verdicts.checked: NCT01703988 posted results confirm frequencyThreshold=0 (all TEAEs reported, so zero is a true zero) and arms 'Nusinersen 3 mg' n=8, 6 mg n=8, 9 mg n=9, 12 mg n=9. I enumerated all 89 otherEvents and all 3 seriousEvents terms: no hydrocephalus, ventricular, macrocephaly, intracranial-pressure, CSF-pressure or papilloedema term at any dose. 0_of_8 at 3 mg is correct, as is 'no events at every dose from 3 to 12 mg'. Mean treatment duration 82.9 days matches the posted timeframe.
verdicts.problem: Cosmetic: the parenthetical in source_table ('only Skin papilloma matched any ventricular/CSF search term') is a search artefact - 'papilloma' matching a 'papilledema' pattern - and reads as if a relevant event were found. It should be removed.

verdicts.checked: NCT04089566 (DEVOTE) otherEvents[6] term='Intracranial pressure increased': EG003 'Part B: Later-Onset SMA: 12/12 mg' 0/8; EG004 'Part B: Later-Onset SMA: 50/28 mg' 1/16 = 6.3%. Exact, and frequencyThreshold=0 is confirmed in the record so the zero is real. Grade 0 correct.

NCT04089566 otherEvents[154] term='CSF pressure increased', organSystem='Investigations': EG005 'Part C: 50/28 mg Nusinersen' 2/40 = 5.0%; zero in all five other groups. Exact. Part C is single-arm so 'no_concurrent_control_arm' is correct.
verdicts.problem: Grade inconsistent with CMS1236 in the same batch. CMS1236 grades asymptomatic raised lumbar opening pressure (12/34, >=28 cmH2O) as 1, with the explicit rationale that 'a raised opening pressure without symptoms, papilloedema or imaging change does not meet the grade-2 definition'. This row grades the same phenomenon - a non-serious 'Investigations' AE of raised CSF pressure, with no reported symptoms, imaging or outcome - as 2, citing a 'raised-ICP band' that is not in the rubric. One of the two must move. On the rubric as written, grade 1 is the consistent value here.

verdicts.checked: NCT03225833 otherEvents[43] term='CSF lymphocyte count increase', organSystem='Investigations': EG005 'WVE-120101 (32 mg)' 1/10 = 10.0%; EG000 'Pooled Placebo' 0/16; zero at 2/4/8/16 mg. Exact. Grade 1 correct.
verdicts.problem: exposure_duration 'up_to_210d' is wrong for this arm. The record's AE timeframe reads 'Day 1 to end of study (Day 196 [32 mg cohort] or Day 210 [all other cohorts])'; this is the 32 mg cohort, so 196 days.

verdicts.checked: NCT03225833 seriousEvents[3] term='Ataxia', organSystem='Nervous system disorders': EG005 'WVE-120101 (32 mg)' 1/10 = 10.0%; 0 in pooled placebo (n=16) and 0 at all four lower doses. verdicts.problem: Same exposure_duration error as CMS1404: the 32 mg cohort ran to Day 196, not Day 210.

verdicts.checked: NCT00607373 otherEvents[72] term='Headache', organSystem='Nervous system disorders': EG001 'Mipomersen' 5/34 = 14.7%; EG000 'Placebo' 2/17 = 11.8%. Exact including the array index. Arm description confirms 'mipomersen 200 mg as a subcutaneous injection once a week for 26 weeks', so dose and exposure_duration are sourced. frequencyThreshold=0. NCT01960348 (APOLLO) otherEvents[32] term='Paraesthesia': EG000 'Patisiran (ALN-TTR02)' 8/148 = 5.4% (23 events); EG001 'Placebo' 3/77 = 3.9% (5 events). Exact. Timeframe confirms 'through End of Study (Day 567)'. Grade 0 correct.

NCT02310906 otherEvents[78] term='Lethargy': EG005 'Part 2a: Total Golodirsen Group' 2/25 = 8.0%; EG006 'Part 2b: Untreated Group (Natural History of Non-exon 53)' 1/14 = 7.1%. Exact. The comparator caveat the row states - an unrandomised, genotype-unmatched untreated natural-history group rather than placebo - is exactly what the arm labels say. Grade 0 correct.

NCT03399370 seriousEvents[220] term='Headache': EG000 'Inclisiran' 1/781 = 0.1%; EG001 'Saline Solution' 1/778 = 0.1%. Exact. Arm description confirms inclisiran sodium 300 mg SC over 18 months. Fetched Lovett A et al., Muscle Nerve 2025;71(6):1006-1015 via PMC12060635 (full text). Results section states verbatim: 'Two participants (1.4%) experienced SAEs of aseptic meningitis, both related to tofersen as assessed by the Investigator.' Every other field checks out exactly - baseline CSF WBC 0-2 and protein 32-67.5, 5 to 7 doses before onset, CSF WBC 144-317 and protein 95-185 during the event, treatment with empiric antibiotics/antivirals/methylprednisolone/analgesics, one continued and one discontinued (Table 1 participants 7 and 8), 147 exposed, 312.56 participant-years, 15 Jul 2022 cut, 'No similar events were experienced by participants receiving placebo'. Grade 2 and direction are right.
verdicts.problem: readout_value is 3.1 pct_incidence. The paper reports 1.4% (2/147). The row's own effect_vs_control field says '2 of 147', which is 1.36% - so the row contradicts itself. The string '3.1' does not appear anywhere in the article; the only percentages in it are 1.4, 2.7, 6.8, 8.8, 16.3, 24.5, 79.6, 89.7 and 98.6. 3.1% is the value of CMS1395 (1/32 aseptic meningitis in NCT03070119), which looks like the source of the copy. As filed the row overstates a labelled tofersen adverse reaction by 2.3-fold.

correction.effect_vs_control: 1.4pct (2 of 147) on tofersen 100 mg vs 0 events on placebo

verdicts.checked: Same article, Results: 'of the 147 participants exposed to tofersen 100 mg, 79.6% had at least 1 CSF WBC value > 10 cells/uL and 89.7% had a shift to high in CSF protein.' Exact. The note's local-lab ULN range of 30-60 mg/dL is confirmed in the Methods. Grade 1 for an isolated CSF-protein elevation is correct.
verdicts.problem: Cosmetic: readout_name 'CSF_total_protein' with readout_value 89.7 reads like a concentration until you reach readout_unit='pct_incidence'. The value is a shift-to-high incidence, not a protein level.

verdicts.checked: Same article, Table 1 'Summary of Participant Narratives', participant 3: event myelitis, clinical features 'Asymptomatic (hospitalized for CSF pleocytosis; imaging findings suggested myelitis)', investigator relatedness 'Related', 7 doses prior to event, baseline CSF WBC 1 cells/uL, baseline CSF protein 44 mg/dL, CSF WBC during event 23 (rising to 94 after 2 weeks), CSF protein during event 58 (rising to 149 after 2 weeks), opening pressure 'Not measured/not reported', action 'Continued'. Every field in the row and its note matches the table cell for cell. Grade 2 for the pleocytosis is correct.

Fetched Miller TM et al., JAMA Neurol via PMC12723595; article-id block confirms PMID 41661214 and doi 10.1001/jamaneurol.2025.4946 exactly as cited. Results subsection 'Cerebrospinal Fluid SOD1 Protein': 'Early reductions in CSF SOD1 concentrations were sustained at week 148, with a reduction of 21% and 25% in the early-start and placebo/delayed-start groups, respectively' and 'became apparent by approximately 8 weeks'. Exact. Direction 'decrease' with grade 0 is correct - target engagement, not toxicity.

Same article, Table 3 'Summary of Adverse Events', VALOR and OLE Tofersen 100 mg (N=104): 'Serious neurologic events 9 (8.7)', broken down as Myelitis 4 (3.9), Papilledema 3 (2.9), Aseptic meningitis 2 (1.9), Radiculitis 1 (1.0). Footnote e matches the note verbatim. Body text confirms '9 participants (8.7%) reported 10 serious neurological AEs... manageable with local standard of care and resolved. One myelitis event and 1 chemical meningitis event led to treatment discontinuation.' Exposure figures confirmed: 104 of 108, 305.35 participant-years, median 181.71 weeks, OLE completed August 2024, median follow-up opportunity 4.9 years. Grade 2 correct.
verdicts.problem: This row is the model for data-cut handling in the batch: it states outright that it is a different cut and population from the 147-participant Muscle & Nerve rows and that the two are not additive. The reciprocal note is missing from CMS1501/CMS1509/CMS1518.

verdicts.checked: Fetched via PMC13004686; article-ids confirm PMID 41634391 and doi 10.1038/s41591-025-04193-6. Results subsection 'Part B cohort with infantile-onset SMA: neurodegeneration': 'Reduction in plasma neurofilament light chain (NfL) levels from baseline at day 183 were significantly greater in the 50/28 mg group (94% reduction) compared with the ENDEAR matched sham group (32% reduction) (P < 0.0001)'. Exact, including the referenced Table 2 and Fig. 2b. Direction 'decrease' with grade 0 is the correct NfL handling. The comparator is correctly identified as the ENDEAR matched SHAM, and the row correctly warns that the sham arm also falls 32% (age-related NfL decline in infants), so the drug effect is the difference, not the raw 94%.

Same article, Table 3 'Parts B and C: overall safety summary', Part B infantile-onset columns: AE leading to death 10 (20.0) for 50/28 mg (n=50) vs 11 (55.0) for Matched sham (ENDEAR) (n=20). Exact. The claim that every rate is at or below the matched sham holds across the whole column (any AE 90.0 vs 100; treatment-related AE 6.0 vs 20.0; SAE 60.0 vs 95.0; treatment-related SAE 0 vs 0; AE leading to death 20.0 vs 55.0). Body text confirms 'only one participant in the Part B infantile-onset 12/12 mg group experienced a treatment-related SAE (respiratory failure)' and the 50.06 / 21.44 participant-year figures. Grade 0 with direction 'decrease' is correct.

Fetched via PMC10287562. Section 'Primary endpoint of safety': 'Adverse events (AEs) were reported in 94% of participants treated with MAPTRx and 75% of participants treated with placebo; all events were considered mild (88%) or moderate (12%) in severity'. Discussion confirms 'AEs considered potentially related to study drug... 15 (44%) versus 0'. Table 1 header confirms the cohort sizes exactly as the note states: placebo N=12, MAPTRx N=34, 10 mg monthly N=6, 30 mg monthly N=6, 60 mg monthly Q4W N=9, 115 mg quarterly N=13. 13-week treatment plus 23-week post-treatment confirmed. Both arms received real intrathecal bolus administrations, so the comparison is LP-matched and the excess is not a sham artefact. Grade 1 correct.
verdicts.problem: redistribution is wrong. The PMC permissions block reads 'https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/ ... Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 International License'. This is a CC-BY article and the schema, and the dataset's own SOURCES-CNS.md rights table, require redistribution='cc_by' for it. Filing it as summary_stat is an under-claim that silently forfeits the right to republish the raw values. It is the only CC-BY article in the batch - the other seven journal sources I licence-checked are CC-BY-NC-ND, Thieme all-rights-reserved, NEJM, an NIHMS author manuscript, or Springer exclusive-licence, all correctly summary_stat.

verdicts.checked: Fetched via PMC12920120; article-ids confirm PMID 41673497 and doi 10.1038/s43587-025-01031-9. Table 3 'Summary of TEAEs during the LTE (safety population)', N=33: 'Participants with >=1 AE, n (%) 31 (93.9)'. Exact. Every claim in the long note is verbatim-accurate against the source: 4 (12.1%) serious TEAEs all assessed as unrelated to treatment or procedure; 3 (9.1%) discontinuations comprising four events (one participant with paranoia and aggression, two with dementia Alzheimer's type); one of those four (dementia Alzheimer's type) possibly related to study treatment; one severe TEAE (pain in extremity); no deaths; 24 (72.7%) with at least one procedure-related event, all mild or moderate and non-serious; and the full common-event list (back pain 39.4, pain in extremity 27.3, headache 24.2, dizziness 15.2, procedural pain 15.2, confusional state 12.1, fatigue 12.1, post-LP syndrome 12.1). CC-BY-NC-ND, so summary_stat is correct. Grade 1 correct, and the procedural dominance of the AE profile is properly recorded.

Full text is paywalled (Nature Medicine, 'under exclusive licence to Springer Nature'), no PMC deposit. Fetched the PubMed record for PMID 41876647: Nat Med. 2026 Apr;32(4):1421-1431, doi 10.1038/s41591-026-04262-4 - both identifiers real and exactly as cited. summary:
55 clinical rows checked against re-fetched primary sources: 14 ClinicalTrials.gov records via the v2 API, 5 FDA prescribing informations via DailyMed, the EMA Qalsody EPAR (EMA/276404/2024) and the EMA Spinraza SmPC (EU/1/17/1188) as PDFs, 8 journal articles as PMC full text, and 3 PubMed abstracts where no full text exists. Verdicts: 33 CONFIRMED, 13 CONFIRMED_MINOR, 1 REFUTED, 8 UNVERIFIABLE. Severity: 32 none, 21 minor, 2 major. 

The one REFUTED row is CMS1501: tofersen aseptic meningitis is filed at 3.1 pct_incidence when Lovett 2025 (Muscle & Nerve 2025;71(6):1006-1015, PMC12060635) states 'Two participants (1.4%) experienced SAEs of aseptic meningitis'. The row's own effect_vs_control field ('2 of 147') contradicts its readout_value; 3.1% is the value of CMS1395 (1/32 in NCT03070119), so this looks like a cross-row copy. The correct value is 1.4. Everything else in that row - the CSF ranges, dose counts, relatedness, placebo comparison, participant-years and data cut - is verbatim-exact. 

The other major-severity finding is CMS1597, a grading rather than a value problem: a +1.2 percentage-point difference from placebo in plasma NfL is graded 1 with effect_direction 'increase' under a curator-invented threshold rule ('>=+10 points -> 2; >0 -> 1; <=0 -> 0'). A 1.2-point difference is noise, and because this is a stated rule it will have produced the same false-positive grade wherever the lane applied it. 

Findings against the four attack grounds I was given: (1) NUMERATOR/DENOMINATOR/COMPARATOR - every one of the 20 ClinicalTrials.gov-sourced rows reproduces exactly, including array indices, arm labels and both denominators. All ten rows where the drug rate sits at or below the concurrent control (CMS1138 45.8 vs 44.4, CMS1334 14.7 vs 11.8, CMS1343 5.4 vs 3.9, CMS1360 8.0 vs 7.1, CMS1369 40.0 vs 58.3, CMS1430 0.1 vs 0.1, CMS1439 7.6 vs 6.4, CMS1544 20 vs 55, CMS1254 and CMS1315 zero-event arms) are correctly graded 0. No manufactured toxicity of that kind was found. (2) PROCEDURE VERSUS DRUG - the two sham-controlled rows (CMS1536, CMS1544, both DEVOTE vs the ENDEAR matched sham) are efficacy and mortality endpoints where the sham comparison favours the drug, so no procedural inflation is possible; both name the sham explicitly. CMS1492 (MAPTRx) is LP-matched on both arms. CMS1571 (BIIB080 LTE) correctly reports that 72.7% of participants had procedure-related events and that back pain and post-LP syndrome dominate. One row needs the attribution added: CMS1168 grades nusinersen arachnoiditis 2 while quoting SmPC section 4.4, which introduces arachnoiditis as 'a risk of adverse reactions occurring as part of the lumbar puncture procedure'. (3) NfL DIRECTION - all seven NfL rows are correct. Falls after HTT-, SOD1- and FUS-lowering ASOs are graded 0 with 'decrease' (CMS1527 -82.8% CSF, CMS1536 -94% plasma, CMS1606 -7.1 points); treatment-emergent rises above concurrent placebo are graded 2 and 1 with 'increase' (CMS1263 +1161 ng/L vs +324 placebo, CMS1298 16.553 vs 12.233); the BIIB105 futility discontinuation is graded 0 with 'no_change' and is explicitly NOT treated as a neurotoxicity grade 3 (CMS1465). No NfL row is filed with direction TBD. This is the single cleanest result in the batch. (4) DATA-CUT CONFUSION - handled on one side of each pair only; see systematic_issues. (5) PROVENANCE KIND - no mislabelled provenance found. Every row that read a number from an abstract says 'abstract' in source_table (CMS1236, CMS1474, CMS1527, CMS1579); the review-sourced row says so and flags the press-release chain underneath (CMS1483); the press-release row says so (CMS1465). (6) REDISTRIBUTION - no over-claims. All FDA, EMA and ClinicalTrials.gov rows are public_domain, correctly. I read the licence statement in each journal source: seven are CC-BY-NC-ND, Thieme all-rights-reserved, NEJM, an NIHMS author manuscript or Springer exclusive-licence, all correctly summary_stat. The single mismatch is the opposite of an over-claim: CMS1492 (Mummery 2023, Nat Med) is CC BY 4.0 and is filed summary_stat, which forfeits a right the schema and the dataset's own SOURCES-CNS.md rights table say should be recorded as cc_by.
systematic_issues:
1. GREY LITERATURE IS THE LARGEST UNVERIFIABLE BLOCK, AND IT CARRIES DISPROPORTIONATE GRADE WEIGHT. Seven of the eight UNVERIFIABLE rows (CMS1325, CMS1597, CMS1606, CMS1614, CMS1623, CMS1632, CMS1641) cite Roche/Genentech medical-affairs slide decks on medically.gene.com and medically.roche.com, and the eighth (CMS1465) cites a Biogen investor press release. None is retrievable: every URL pattern returns 404 or 503, the portals are JS-gated with no sitemap, and the decks are explicitly marked 'preliminary analyses performed on non-final data set'. redistribution='verify' is set correctly on all of them, which is good practice. But these rows are not peripheral - CMS1632 is the load-bearing tominersen ventriculomegaly row at the phase 3 grain (24.3% vs 11.4% vBSI) and CMS1325 is the row the curator says 'matters disproportionately because it shows the SYMPTOMATIC case count understates the imaging signal roughly fivefold'. Where I could cross-check them against the public registry the divergences are consistent with different data cuts rather than transcription error (CMS1623's 7.7 vs 5.8 on n=260 against the registry's 7.6 vs 6.4 on n=263/264), with one exception: CMS1641 asserts a 'Meningitis chemical' event that does not exist as a preferred term anywhere in the final NCT03761849 posting, which instead posts 'Meningitis aseptic' 1/263. Recommendation: label the whole grey-literature class as unverifiable-by-a-third-party in the row itself, not just via the rights column, and prefer the registry row wherever one exists. This extrapolates to the 43 CHDI-2021, 12 CHDI-2023, 2 CHDI-2022 and 3 press-release rows the source registry counts across the clinical lane - about 60 rows, roughly an eighth of the clinical set.

2. A MECHANICAL '>0 MEANS GRADE 1' THRESHOLD MANUFACTURES TOXICITY FROM NOISE. CMS1597 and CMS1606 both state the rule verbatim: '>=+10 points -> 2 (treatment-emergent axonal-injury signal); >0 -> 1; <=0 -> 0'. Applied to a +1.2 percentage-point plasma NfL difference from placebo, it yields a grade-1 neurotoxicity label with effect_direction 'increase' for a difference no one would call a signal. The rule ignores dispersion entirely. The same weakness shows up without a stated rule at CMS1263, where grade 2 rests on a mean of +1161 ng/L with SD 2980 on n=9 - a standard error near 1000 against an 837 ng/L excess over placebo - and at CMS1272, where grade 1 rests on a curator-computed +2.67 mL versus +0.88 mL with no posted dispersion for the change and no statistical test. Every one of these rows flags its own fragility in notes and carries grade_provisional, which is honest, but the grade field itself does not encode the uncertainty and that is what a model trains on. Recommendation: any continuous-endpoint grade above 0 should require separation from the concurrent control, not merely a larger point estimate; where dispersion is unavailable the grade should be capped or the row marked low-confidence in a structured field.

3. DATA-CUT CROSS-REFERENCES ARE ASYMMETRIC. The lane clearly understands the problem - CMS1562 says outright 'DIFFERENT DATA CUT AND DIFFERENT POPULATION from the 147-participant Muscle & Nerve rows - the two sets are not additive', and CMS1244 and CMS1280 both carry 'Flagged for the assembler to de-duplicate against the tofersen label-extraction lane'. But the marker is only ever on one side of the pair. The three Lovett rows (CMS1501/1509/1518, N=147, cut 15 Jul 2022) carry no reciprocal pointer back to Miller 2026 (N=104, cut Aug 2024); CMS1623 is marked 'duplicate_also_in_lane=clinical_programs' while its registry counterpart CMS1439 is not. The tofersen neuro-AE tally in particular now exists at five overlapping grains in this batch alone - the QALSODY label's undifferentiated 'four patients', EPAR Table 37 (papilloedema 7/147, myelitis 4/147, aseptic meningitis 6/147 at 28 Feb 2023), EPAR Table 38 related SAEs (3/147 ICP increased), ClinicalTrials.gov NCT03070119 per-group counts, Lovett's 10 participants/12 events at 15 Jul 2022, and Miller's 9 participants/10 events at Aug 2024. A consumer summing any two of these double-counts the same patients. Recommendation: make the cross-reference a structured bidirectional field (e.g. same_events_as=<measurement_id list>) rather than free text on whichever row was curated second.

4. ONE GRADING RULE IS APPLIED TWO DIFFERENT WAYS TO THE SAME PHENOMENON. Raised intracranial/CSF opening pressure without symptoms is graded 1 at CMS1236 with an explicit rationale ('a raised opening pressure without symptoms, papilloedema or imaging change does not meet the grade-2 definition') and graded 2 at CMS1457 citing a 'raised-ICP band' that does not exist in the rubric - even though CMS1457 is a non-serious Investigations-SOC AE with no reported symptoms or imaging. The rubric's grade-2 examples are aseptic meningitis, radiculitis, myelitis and papilledema; raised pressure per se is not among them. Because raised ICP is one of the two named priority endpoints for this dataset, this inconsistency will propagate widely. Recommendation: write the rule down once - asymptomatic pressure elevation = 1, pressure elevation with papilloedema, symptoms, imaging change or serious-AE status = 2, requiring intervention = 3 - and re-sweep every intracranial_pressure and CSF_pressure row against it.

5. DOSE AND ANATOMY ARE OCCASIONALLY SUPPLIED FROM OUTSIDE THE CITED LOCUS. CMS1343 records patisiran 0.3 mg/kg against NCT01960348, whose record contains no 'mg/kg' string anywhere; CMS1289 grades hydrocephalus 3 on the strength of a shunt reported in Stoker 2021, which is named in notes but absent from source_ref and source_table; CMS1199 assigns cns_region 'brainstem' to a label row for vertigo that the label does not localise. Each value is defensible in itself, but the falsifiable claim the schema makes - this number is at this place in this document - is not true of them. Recommendation: any field not readable at the cited locus needs its own citation, not a mention in notes.

6. WHAT IS WORKING, AND SHOULD BE PRESERVED. Numerator/denominator/comparator fidelity on registry rows is essentially perfect across 20 rows; the at-or-below-control-means-grade-0 rule is applied consistently across ten rows and no alarming-sounding term was inflated; NfL direction is right on all seven NfL rows including the futility-not-toxicity case; provenance kind is declared honestly on every abstract-, review- and press-release-sourced row; and rights are read from the licence statement in the document rather than assumed from the publisher, with CC-BY-NC-ND correctly refused an upgrade to cc_by. The one rights defect (CMS1492) is an under-claim, not a legal exposure. Whatever process produced these habits should be left alone.
